candidates.angle: स्थित्वा, established, and its promise that death cannot break it
candidates.evidence: स्थित्वा (having remained established) ... अन्तकालेऽपि (even at the end of life)

candidates.angle: The brahmic state ends all delusion for good
candidates.evidence: नैनां प्राप्य विमुह्यति (having reached it, one is never deluded)

candidates.angle: The word ब्राह्मी names the state of Brahman itself
candidates.evidence: एषा ब्राह्मी स्थितिः (this is the Brahmic state)

en.intro: Krishna has just finished describing a mind at peace with itself. Now he gives this state a name, and with it a guarantee that even death cannot take it away.
en.notice: Krishna names the brahmic state: once reached, delusion ends, and even at death it holds.
en.next: Arjuna now asks why Krishna urges him to fight if understanding is better than action.
en.meaning: Arjuna, this is the Brahmic state. Having reached it, one is never deluded. Remaining established in it even at the end of life, one attains freedom in the supreme reality.

hi.body: हे पार्थ, यह ब्राह्मी स्थिति है। इसे प्राप्त होकर मनुष्य कभी मोहित नहीं होता। इस स्थिति में अंतकाल में भी स्थित हो जाने पर ब्रह्मनिर्वाण प्राप्त हो जाता है। यह ब्राह्मी स्थिति है; अंत समय में भी मिले तो ब्रह्म-निर्वाण अर्जुन अब पूछते हैं कि यदि ज्ञान कर्म से बेहतर है, तो कृष्ण उन्हें इस भयानक कर्म के लिए क्यों कहते हैं।

borrowed: "Arjuna now asks why Krishna urges him to fight if understanding is better than action." (The phrase 'understanding is better than action' (ज्ञान कर्म से बेहतर है) is Arjuna's specific objection from the next verse (3.1). In verse 72, Krishna is actually giving a guarantee that the state is permanent and even death cannot undo it. The script incorrectly presents Arjuna's specific question as Krishna's ongoing message in this verse.)

contrast_template: "कृष्ण ने अभी मन की शांति का वर्णन किया है, न कि युद्ध की तैयारी का।" (The intro uses the Hindi contrast 'न कि' ('not X but Y') to contrast 'peace of mind' with 'preparation for war'. However, the SOURCE verse does not contrast these two things; it simply names the 'Brahmic state'. The previous verse (71) was about peace, but this verse (72) is about naming that state, not contrasting it with war preparation.)
